transcript.text: My Beko keeps stopping randomly in the middle of a wash with water still in it. Sometimes it's fine for a week, then it does it twice in a day. The model starts WTG I think. I've cleaned the filter. Driving me mad.

That sounds most like an intermittent drain problem. Even with a clean filter, a Beko can stop mid-cycle if it cannot empty within a set time. It may then leave water in the drum and appear to have “randomly” stopped.

Things to check, in order:

1. When it stops, try a Drain/Spin programme
• If it drains and spins normally afterwards, the fault may be intermittent.
• If it just hums, drains very slowly, or does nothing, suspect the drain pump, something around the pump impeller, or the drain hose.

2. Check the pump impeller, not just the filter
• Switch off at the socket and unplug first.
• With the filter removed, look into the opening with a torch. There is usually a small impeller at the back.
• It should turn with a little resistance/clicking, but not be jammed or excessively loose/wobbly.
• Small items—bra wire, hair grips, coins, fabric, socks—can sit beyond the filter and only obstruct it occasionally.

3. Check the drain hose and waste connection
• Make sure the hose is not kinked, crushed behind the machine, or pushed too far down the standpipe.
• Check the sink trap/waste pipe if it drains into the plumbing under a sink. A partial blockage there can cause intermittent draining.
• If the hose goes into a standpipe, it should not be sealed airtight and should be at the correct height (normally roughly 40–100 cm from the floor; exact requirement is in the manual).

4. **Notice where in the wash it stops
• Stops before the first spin / at rinse with water left in it: usually drainage.
• Stops with no water left, door locked, or showing a code: could be a door lock, motor issue, pressure sensor, or control fault.
• Stops only on large/heavy loads and then eventually spins: possibly an out-of-balance load issue rather than a fault.

5. Look for an error code or flashing lights
   Beko models often show a code such as E01/E02/E03 or a combination of flashing LEDs. Photograph it before switching off—this is very useful for identifying the fault. Drain-related errors are often associated with pump/drain issues, though codes vary by exact model.

Given the “fine for a week, then twice in a day” pattern, an ageing drain pump** is quite plausible. They can work when cold or when the obstruction shifts, then fail intermittently. Cleaning the filter alone won’t always reveal that.

Don’t keep repeatedly running it with water in the drum or leave it unattended. If it is under warranty, book Beko service rather than dismantling it. Otherwise, a repairer can usually confirm a pump fault fairly quickly.

If you can tell me:
• the full model number from the sticker inside the door or on the back (it will be longer than “WTG”),
• whether it hums when it should be draining,
• and any error code/lights,

I can narrow it down much more.

The sticker inside the door is so faded I can't read it, and I've no receipt, so all I've got is the WTG. When it stops there's water in the drum and the time just freezes. Sometimes a light flashes that I think is the start light, but there's no proper code. The pump does sometimes run for a few seconds and then stop. The hose is fine, it goes into a standpipe. If I switch it off and on it sometimes carries on and finishes, other times it stalls again. I've not tried a drain/spin programme, and I'm not taking panels off.

You don’t need the full model number to narrow this down. With water left in the drum, the displayed time freezing, and the pump sometimes running briefly then stopping, the most likely cause is still an intermittent draining fault:

• something intermittently catching in/behind the pump,
• a pump that is failing when warm or under load,
• less commonly, a partial blockage in the standpipe/waste plumbing.

Restarting sometimes making it continue is quite typical of a marginal pump or obstruction moving position.

### The useful no-panels test
Next time it stops, don’t restart it straight away. Turn the programme selector to Drain & Spin (or just Drain, if yours has it), press Start, and observe:

• It drains quickly and completes: could be an intermittent pump/obstruction, but also possibly a programme/control issue.
• Pump hums/runs but little or no water comes out: likely a blockage or weak pump.
• Pump runs for a few seconds then cuts out, repeatedly: strongly points to the pump struggling, overheating, or detecting that it cannot drain.
• Absolutely no pump noise: could be pump wiring/control, but a failed pump is still common.

Don’t leave it attempting this for ages if it clearly isn’t draining; switch it off.

### Things you can safely do without removing panels
1. Re-check the filter with a torch, with the machine unplugged.
   Since you have already cleaned it, look beyond it for anything caught near the impeller. You do not have to dismantle the machine. If you can see the little impeller, it should move with a slight magnetic “stepped” resistance, rather than being solidly stuck. Don’t force it.

2. Check the standpipe behaviour.
   While it is trying to drain, look/listen at the standpipe:
• Water backs up, gurgles heavily, or spills out: likely a plumbing/standpipe restriction.
• No water arrives at all: likely machine-side drainage/pump.

   Even if the hose looks fine, the standpipe can be partly blocked farther down.

3. Avoid repeated resets as a long-term workaround.
   Turning it off and back on can temporarily reset a pump thermal cut-out or the machine’s drain-time fault, but it won’t cure the cause.

The flashing Start/Pause light is often the machine indicating that the programme has paused or cannot proceed; without a display code it isn’t specific enough on its own.

### Likely repair
If the Drain & Spin test is inconsistent, a repairer would normally check the drain path and then replace the drain pump if needed. It is usually a relatively routine repair, and much more likely than an expensive main-board failure given your symptoms.

When booking someone, describe it as: “Beko WTG-series washer intermittently stops with water in drum; timer freezes; drain pump runs briefly then stops; filter and external hose checked; reset sometimes lets it finish.” That should steer them straight to the drain system/pump rather than a general call-out.
